title: VPC Topology HealthGate terraform module: subnet lifecycle, NAT pooling, endpoints & rolling upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (vpc_topology_healthgate) that manages subnet lifecycle, multi-tenant NAT/IGW pooling, VPC endpoints, route tables, and automated health-driven upgrade hooks for Private/VPC deployments. The module must include preflight/postflight checks, safe state-migration strategies, and observability hooks for Redwood Console.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs for subnet tiers (control/data/infra), CIDR allocation strategy, NAT pool sizing, and endpoint policies
Rolling upgrade plan: canary apply on a single AZ, automated rollback on healthcheck failures, and state snapshots persisted to S3/GCS before disruptive ops
Integrated health probes: synthetic egress/intra-subnet reachability and route blackhole detection with auto-heal primitives (recreate route/replace NAT)
Backward-compatible Terraform major/minor upgrade strategy documented and validated (state migration examples)
Cost tagging and egress accounting hooks emit tags for per-tenant NAT usage and feed into Redwood Console metrics
Module unit tests (terragrunt/terrform tests) and integration runbook with GitHub Actions pipeline are present
technical_notes: Module layout: modules/subnet, modules/egress_pool, modules/endpoints, modules/routing, modules/health_probes
Use registry-style inputs + feature flags (enable_nat_pooling, enable_endpoint_policy_enforcement) to preserve backwards compatibility
NAT pooling: implement per-tenant pool with dynamic size based on concurrency estimate; expose allocator outputs (nat_gateway_ids, public_ips) for downstream resources
State migration: provide examples for moving from single IGW NAT to NAT pool using terraform state mv + plan-based dry-run snapshots stored in S3 with versioning
Health probes: Lambda-based synthetic probes that validate outbound connectivity, DNS resolution, and path to S3 endpoints; probes emit metrics via CloudWatch/Prometheus and trigger SNS for rollbacks

Routing safety: route-table reconciliation routine that compares desired vs observed route CIDRs, marks suspect routes as "blackhole" and attempts repair by replacing route target or re-creating route in a canary AZ before global remediation
Canary upgrades: implement destroy-recreate canary in single subnet with traffic-shifting annotation; use remote-exec + smoke tests before promoting change
IAM & endpoints: support endpoint policy enforcement via IAM condition templates and explicit allow lists for private S3/Dynamo/Gateway endpoints
Observability: hook module outputs into Redwood Console via a lightweight telemetry lambda that forwards per-subnet latency, egress cost tags, and probe failures
Testing: GH Actions matrix across tf versions (1.4, 1.6), provider variations (aws v4.x/v5.x) and terratest for integration; include chaos test to simulate NAT failure and validate auto-heal
